recommendations.regimenLabel: Analgesia + antiemetic for the acute episode
steps: Analgesia (NSAID/opioid) and antiemetics for the acute episode.
USS to confirm gallstones; check LFTs (exclude CBD stone/cholecystitis).
Low-fat dietary advice while awaiting surgery.
Elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic gallstones.
Escalate if fever, persistent pain or jaundice (cholecystitis/cholangitis).

drugRefs.freq: up to twice daily as needed
drugRefs.why: NSAIDs are effective first-line for biliary colic and may reduce progression to cholecystitis. Avoid in renal impairment/peptic ulcer disease.
For pain not controlled by an NSAID; titrate to effect.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Diseases of the Gallbladder and Bile Ducts
NICE CG188 — Gallstone Disease: Diagnosis and Management

confirm: Postprandial RUQ/epigastric pain ± radiation to scapula, lasting <6 h, with gallstones on US and no fever/inflammation.
